lead.headline: The Iran-US Shadow War Just Went Hot — and Gulf Oil Is the Hostage
lead.they_say: The US and Iran are engaged in containable, tit-for-tat strikes that won't disrupt global energy markets.
lead.reality: Iranian drones hit Kuwait International Airport on June 3. The conflict crossed an infrastructure-targeting threshold. Gulf states are now directly in the line of fire — not watching from the sidelines. The OECD has already flagged a 'dark scenario' for prolonged Gulf energy crisis.
lead.actors: US Central Command, IRGC, Kuwait, OPEC+

stories.headline: Anthropic's $1 Trillion Valuation Proves the AI Bubble Is Just Getting Started
stories.they_say: AI valuations have peaked. A correction is overdue and healthy.
stories.reality: Anthropic is pursuing a US share sale at a near-$1tn valuation. Compute concentration is accelerating, not deflating. The AI rally has decoupled from geopolitical sell-offs — it has its own gravity now. The semiconductor supply chain is the new oil pipeline.

stories.headline: The Dollar's Grip Weakens: Yen at 160 Forces Japan's Hand
stories.they_say: Currency markets are orderly. The yen's decline reflects fundamental rate differentials.
stories.reality: USD/JPY has returned to 160 — the exact level that triggered Japan's last intervention. Hong Kong's $550B Exchange Fund is quietly preparing S&P 500 allocations. Capital is fleeing yen exposure. This isn't orderly — it's a slow-motion currency crisis that the petrodollar system can't afford.

stories.headline: Ukraine Is Not Frozen — Seven Dead in Drone Strike on Civilian Bus
stories.they_say: The Ukraine front has stabilized. The conflict is in a manageable stalemate.
stories.reality: A drone killed seven civilians on a bus in Russian-controlled territory. Zelenskyy is asking Trump for long-range missiles after renewed Russian strikes across Ukraine. There is no stalemate — there is a grinding war of attrition that the West is slowly losing the will to fund.

stories.headline: Shell's Nigeria Pipeline Scandal Exposes the ESG Fiction
stories.they_say: Major energy companies have reformed their environmental practices in developing nations.
stories.reality: Internal documents show Shell continued pumping oil through a Nigerian pipeline for years after discovering pollution evidence. The ESG branding was a marketing operation. The operational reality never changed. This is the gap between what corporations say and what they do — and it's the same gap we track in every sector.

stories.headline: China Centralizes Its Mining Empire — The Rare Earth Squeeze Tightens
stories.they_say: Global mineral supply chains are market-driven and decentralized.
stories.reality: Beijing just selected a state firm to centrally coordinate all overseas mining acquisitions. Lithium, rare earths, cobalt — the state-capitalist model is tightening its grip on the minerals that power everything from EVs to semiconductors. The West has no equivalent strategy.

stories.headline: OECD's 'Dark Scenario' Warning Validates What We've Been Saying
stories.they_say: Global economic forecasts remain stable. The Gulf situation is a regional concern.
stories.reality: The OECD — not known for alarmism — formally published a 'dark scenario' linking prolonged Gulf crisis directly to inflation repricing. When the technocrats start using words like 'dark scenario,' the market hasn't priced the risk. Yet.
